title: Iwakuni’s Tsunami Swim Team treads water with Japanese Fitness Ocean Swim Team (Package/Pkg)
description: Marine Corps Air Station Iwakuni swimmers left more than a splash during the Friendship Swim Meet against the Japanese Fitness Ocean Swim Team. Marine Corporal Kate Busto made some waves to show you how the swimmers bonded. This story includes soundbites from Annastacia Kirk, Tsunami Swim Team, and Hayato Yamashita, Fitness Ocean Swim Team. This story is also available in high definition.

- [Reporter] The Marine Corps Air Station Iwakuni's
Tsunami Swim Team dived into their latest competition
during the Friendship Swim Meet.
The team participated with a local Japanese swim team
called Fitness Ocean Swim.
- 'Cause we live in Japan and we get to have
great opportunities to swim against the Japanese
and talk to them.
Like today I talked to a lot of Japanese people,
and asked them,
"Hey! How are old are you? What's your name?"
I think it's a great opportunity to swim with them.
- [Team] Let's go!
- [Reporter] The American and Japanese swimmers
use this swim meet as a way
to strengthen Japanese-American relations.
- The event like today the only time we interact
with Americans,
so it was good.
Through swimming, Japan and the United States
can get along well together.
- [Reporter] Even though the two teams share
different nationalities,
they both felt the same about the competition.
- The distance and depth of the swimming pool
was completely different,
so I was a little bit nervous.
- I mean, I always get nervous every meet,
so I just talk to myself like,
"You've got this. Focus on yourself."
I always stare at the lane.
I'm like, "You've got this, Anna. You've got this."
- [Reporter] The swim teams competed in events
such as the 50 meter freestyle and 200 meter relays.
Reporting from Marine Corps Air Station Iwakuni, Japan,
I'm Marine Corporal Kate Busto.
